steps.say: HLA-B27 is present in 85 to 90 percent of ankylosing spondylitis. Three ideas explain the link, from presented peptides to misfolded chains. This figure shows the spinal damage that follows. Testing is indicated for inflammatory back pain, not mechanical pain.
steps.tx: Axial spondyloarthritis (**axSpA**, inflammatory spine and sacroiliac disease) links strongly to **HLA-B27** (a tissue type protein), present in **85 to 90 percent** of ankylosing spondylitis in Caucasian populations. Three hypotheses explain the link: presentation of arthritogenic self peptides, intracellular heavy chain misfolding with endoplasmic reticulum stress and IL-23 activation, and surface free heavy chain homodimers triggering killer immunoglobulin like receptors. A young patient with chronic back pain requires HLA-B27 testing.

vis.alt: Whole body MRI showing spondylitis, sacroiliitis, and enthesitis in ankylosing spondylitis.
vis.caption: Whole body MRI maps spinal and sacroiliac inflammation in one acquisition. HLA-B27 positivity indicates the workup. Image: Weber et al, CC BY 2.0.

steps.say: Inflammatory back pain has five features and four are required. Onset below 40 with insidious start, exercise relief, rest failure, and night pain define it. Morning stiffness beyond 30 to 45 minutes supports the call. Mechanical pain follows none of these rules.
steps.tx: Night and morning spinal pain that eases with movement is inflammatory back pain (**IBP**). ASAS counts five clues and requires at least **4 of 5**: start below **40 years**, creeping onset, relief with exercise, no relief with rest, and nocturnal pain that lifts on getting up. Stiffness past **30 to 45 minutes** each morning backs the call. Pain that worsens with activity and settles with rest instead points to mechanical causes.

steps.say: ASAS classification needs 3 months of pain starting below 45 years. The imaging arm is sacroiliitis plus one feature. The clinical arm is HLA-B27 plus two features. Either arm is enough for classification.
steps.tx: ASAS axial SpA classification applies with back pain for **3 months** or more starting below **45 years**. The imaging arm requires definite sacroiliitis on imaging (active MRI edema or radiographic damage by modified New York criteria) plus **1 or more** SpA features. The clinical arm requires **HLA-B27** plus **2 or more** other SpA features. Meeting either arm classifies the patient, so a positive MRI with one feature is already enough.

steps.say: Non-radiographic disease has the same burden without X-ray damage. Films lack bilateral grade 2 or unilateral grade 3 change. MRI is the test that indicates the edema films miss. Treatment response is equal in both forms.
steps.tx: Active spinal inflammation with clean radiographs is non radiographic axial SpA (**nr-axSpA**). Films show less than bilateral grade **2** or unilateral grade **3** sacroiliitis, yet STIR MRI exposes subchondral **bone marrow edema** (inflammatory fluid in bone). Suffering and drug response match radiographic ankylosing spondylitis exactly. A normal X-ray therefore never closes the case, and MRI is required before the diagnosis is dismissed.

vis.alt: Sacroiliac ankylosis with vertebral syndesmophytes, stooped posture, and extra-articular manifestations.
vis.caption: Radiographic disease shows ankylosis and posture change while non-radiographic disease needs MRI for proof. Both forms carry equal burden. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Five bedside measures are the trackers of the spine over time. BASDAI and ASDAS are the scores for symptoms while Schober, chest expansion, and wall distance measure movement. A low Schober or a low chest expansion indicates restriction. All five are recorded at every visit.
steps.tx: Spinal assessment uses Bath indices and tape measures together. The Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (**BASDAI**, symptom questionnaire) and Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score (**ASDAS**, with CRP) track activity. Modified **Schober** below **5 cm** indicates restricted lumbar flexion, chest expansion below **2.5 cm** at the fourth intercostal space indicates costovertebral involvement, and occiput to wall distance tracks cervical kyphosis. Falling numbers across visits indicate effective therapy.

steps.say: Continuous NSAIDs at full dose are the first therapy for active axial disease. They relieve symptoms rapidly and may slow bony change. Conventional synthetic DMARDs do not work for pure spinal disease. Biologics follow two failed NSAIDs over 4 weeks.
steps.tx: Full strength nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (**NSAIDs**, prostaglandin blocking painkillers) open therapy for active symptomatic axial SpA, calming pain within days and perhaps braking bony overgrowth. Methotrexate, sulfasalazine, and leflunomide cannot touch purely axial disease. When **2** different **NSAIDs** fail across **4 weeks**, TNF blockade, **IL-17A** blockade (secukinumab, ixekizumab), or dual IL-17A and F blockade with bimekizumab takes over.

steps.say: Disease outside the spine decides prognosis and follow up. Uveitis is seen in 25 to 30 percent of patients. Bowel inflammation, aortic valve leakage, heart block, and apical lung scarring complete the list. This figure is the map of the full territory.
steps.tx: Extra-skeletal disease includes acute unilateral anterior **uveitis** (eye inflammation) in **25 to 30 percent**, settling with topical glucocorticoids, plus subclinical or clinical inflammatory bowel disease. Ascending **aortitis** (aortic wall inflammation) with root dilatation causes aortic regurgitation, cardiac conduction blocks slow the pulse, and apical pulmonary fibrocystic disease invites **Aspergillus** (fungal) colonization. Annual eye, bowel, heart, and lung review is required in established disease.

vis.alt: Diverse axial, peripheral, and extra-articular manifestations of spondyloarthritis.
vis.caption: Eyes, bowel, heart, and lungs are all territory of axial disease. Annual review of each organ is required. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Young chronic back pain with night symptoms is spondylitis until proven otherwise. HLA-B27 and MRI sacroiliac views are the two opening tests. NSAIDs come first and biologics follow failure. Extra-spinal organs are reviewed every year.
steps.tx: Young chronic back pain with night symptoms and morning stiffness is axial SpA until proven otherwise. **HLA-B27** plus MRI sacroiliac views open the workup, ASAS arms classify, and BASDAI with tape measures follows activity. Full dose **NSAIDs** lead therapy while TNF or IL-17 blockade follows 2 failures over **4 weeks**. Eyes, bowel, aortic valve, conduction, and lung apices complete the review, because the spine is only the centre of the disease.
